paragraphs.text: # dsh-github-hub — a GitHub plugin hub for DeepSeek Harness

A native DSH panel (host half + browser half) that signs in to your GitHub account, keeps a
sign-in

history, searches GitHub / npm for `deepseek-harness` (`dsh-plugin`) plugins, and installs
them into

the current profile with one click — through exactly the same path as
**Settings → Plugins** and `d

ofile with one click — through exactly the same path as
**Settings → Plugins** and `dsh plugin add`.
Chinese documentation: README.zh.md
## What it adds

* **Discover** — search GitHub repositories (`topic:dsh-plugin`, `topic:deepseek-harness`,
`dsh-plug

in in:name,description,readme`, …) or npm packages (`keywords:dsh-plugin`).
*Inspect* reads the repo

sitory's `package.json` and tells you whether it really is an
installable DSH plugin (does it declar

e `dsh.bundle.patch`? does it ship a `dsh.client` half?).
*Install* runs the profile's own pnpm path

with a live log, cancel support, and an
"allow the blocked build scripts and retry" button when pnp

m withholds lifecycle scripts.
* **Installed** — the profile's bundles and plugin rows, with enable

/ disable / remove,
load errors and read-only reasons.
* **Account** — sign in with a **Personal Acc

ess Token** or **OAuth Device Flow**
(bring your own OAuth App `client_id`; no client secret needed)

. Sign-in / sign-out history
is persisted and can be cleared.
* **Diagnostics** — a connectivity rep

ort for the GitHub API, npm, DNS, the hosts file, `git`
and `pnpm`, plus which rung of the TLS trust
ladder the current requests use.

Then **restart the desktop app** — reloading the page is not enough, because DSH collects its boot
i

njection table once per host start, and a new plugin's client bundle only enters that manifest on
th

e next start (the web profile needs its `dsh web` process restarted for the same reason).
A **git-br
anch icon** then appears in the left sidebar and opens the panel in the central area.
## Read-only endpoints

Beyond the panel, the host half exposes a few read-only endpoints for troubleshooting (all require
t
he browser session cookie):
| Endpoint | Purpose |
| `GET /dsh-github/state` | account, settings, sign-in history, trust ladder, client-bundle graph st

ate |
| `GET /dsh-github/health` | GitHub API, npm, DNS, hosts, git, pnpm checks plus plain-language

notes |
| `GET /dsh-github/client` | the graph `rev` and real URL of the client bundle, next to the

`rev` computed from the file on disk (a mismatch means edits are not loaded yet) |
| `GET /dsh-gith

ub/search?source=github\|npm&q=…` | search |
| `POST /dsh-github/repo/package` | read a repository's

`package.json` and judge it |
| `POST /dsh-github/inspect` | pre-flight one spec through the real p
lugin manager (performs the GitHub connection check, installs nothing) |
## Verified on this machine
* the GitHub API is reachable through the local accelerator at `tls=default` (144 system roots were

merged into the process default chain at startup), so no insecure rung was needed;
* `pnpm add githu

b:<owner>/<repo>` and `pnpm add git+https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git` both
fetch and link a rea

l package (37s and 19s, peer dependencies included);
* the official pipeline `pluginManager.installB

undle` completed end to end for a `link:` spec
(pnpm log events → progress polling → bundle activati

on);
* `POST /inspect` on `github:<owner>/<repo>` returns `{status:'accepted', kind:'git', host:'git

hub.com'}`;
* the fences hold: authenticated 200, no cookie 401, `sec-fetch-site: cross-site` 403.
## Signing in

* **Token (recommended)** — create one at <https://github.com/settings/tokens> with `read:user`
(add

`repo` for private repositories) and paste it into the panel.
It is stored in the DSH credential se

rvice as the record `dsh-github-hub/github`
(kind `grant`) and is **never** sent to the page; the UI

only shows login, avatar, scopes and
the last four characters.
* **Device flow** — create an OAuth

App (no client secret required), paste its `client_id`,
start the flow, enter the one-time code at <
https://github.com/login/device>.
## Data
| Item | Location |

| GitHub token | DSH credential service (record `dsh-github-hub/github`) |
| Settings + sign-in hist

ory | `$DSH_HOME/.dsh-github-hub.json` (no token, max 200 entries) |
| Install logs | `$DSH_PROFILE_
DIR/.plugin-manager/logs/operation-*/pnpm.log` |

All endpoints live under `ctx.webServer` at `/dsh-github/*` behind three fences: loopback (or
explic

itly trusted) Host, no cross-site requests, and write requests accepted only from the
local machine.
## GitHub behind a local interceptor

Accelerators such as Watt Toolkit / Steam++ rewrite `github.com`, `api.github.com` and
`raw.githubus

ercontent.com` to `127.0.0.1` and re-serve them through a local reverse proxy with
its own CA, which

Node does not trust by default (`unable to verify the first certificate`).
This plugin walks a trus
t ladder instead of failing:

1. default trust chain;
2. default roots **plus** the operating system root store (equivalent to `no

de --use-system-ca`);
3. trust the local interceptor — only when the peer genuinely resolves to loop

back **and** the
setting is enabled, and the UI always reports `tls: local-interceptor` when it happ

**and** the
setting is enabled, and the UI always reports `tls: local-interceptor` when it happens.

Installing from GitHub uses pnpm's `github:owner/repo` (git) transport, so **`git` must be on
PATH**
; the plugin manager performs a bounded connection check before pnpm starts.
## Known limits

* A freshly installed plugin usually still needs an app restart (or page reload) before its
sidebar

icon appears — DSH collects the index injection table once at startup.
* Installing a third-party pl

ugin executes third-party host code inside your DSH process.
The panel shows repository metadata and

the `package.json` verdict, but does not audit code.
* Removing a bundle does not delete data files
the third-party plugin wrote under `$DSH_HOME`.
